cases.question: If an online store can't ship my order in the time it promised, what does federal law say it has to offer me?
cases.answer:
Federal law, specifically $\S 435.2$ of 16 CFR, requires that if a seller is unable to ship merchandise within the time stated in the solicitation, they must offer the buyer, clearly and conspicuously and without prior demand, an option to either consent to a delay in shipping or to cancel the order and receive a prompt refund. This offer must be made within a reasonable time after the seller first becomes aware of the inability to ship, but no later than the original applicable time.

The law also states that if the seller fails to offer this option and has not shipped within the applicable time, it constitutes an unfair method of competition and an unfair or deceptive act or practice.

(Source: ftc_mail_order_rule_16cfr435.xml, $\S 435.2$ Mail, Internet, or telephone order sales.)
